exposure: Extremely preterm (<28 weeks) or very-preterm delivery (28 to <32 weeks)
outcome: Antibiotic resistance to ampicillin and gentamicin
Clinical cofactors associated with culture-proven sepsis and antibiotic resistance
cohort: 266 neonates with sepsis at a tertiary healthcare center in Surabaya, Indonesia
finding: The study identified extremely preterm delivery, late-onset sepsis, cesarean section, and absence of antenatal corticosteroids as factors associated with culture-proven sepsis and resistance to first-line antibiotics.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was associated with increased odds of resistance to first-line antibiotics in neonates with sepsis.
